_comment: COMPUTE-MATCHED depth vs width, WIDE arm.
Same block-steps per token and the same parameter count as
compute-matched.json, with the reuse pattern inverted: 32 stages applied
once each, instead of 4 stages applied 8 times.
looping : head_dim 16, n_heads 8, d_model 128, ffn 384, 4 stages x 8 loops
32 block-steps/token, 919,172 params
wide    : head_dim 16, n_heads 4, d_model  64, ffn  58, 32 stages x 1 loop
32 block-steps/token, 919,648 params
Both model blocks came from examples/param_match.rs. Hand-matching was 50%
wrong on the first attempt: parameters scale ~d^2, and the validator
requires d_model = n_heads * head_dim, so the reachable widths jump from
1.7M to 6.9M with nothing between. The tool searches head_dim, pins both
arms to the same one, then binary-searches ffn_hidden for the last 0.05%.
KNOWN UNCONTROLLED DIFFERENCE: head count 4 vs 8. Not matchable at an 8x
stage ratio, and the tool says so rather than quietly matching on something
else. Rule it out before attributing a win to width.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/compute-matched-wide.json depth gpu 1 --seeds=0,1,2
Compare against compute-matched.json at `depth gpu 8`. Same rung, same steps,
same eval split, same batch.
